title: Introduce token-minting delegation service and audit-friendly token surface
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem: We currently have a mix of long-lived root keys and ad-hoc service tokens that are hard to attribute in audit logs, difficult to rotate without customer impact, and incompatible with our SSO session model. This increases blast radius and slows incident response.

Goal: Design and implement a Token Minting & Delegation Service (TMDS) that issues short-lived, scope-limited tokens with machine- and human-readable metadata for auditability. TMDS should integrate with SSO/SAML sessions, support programmatic delegation (service->service), expose an admin surface for emergency revocation, and emit structured audit events compatible with existing logging pipelines.

Success criteria: (1) All new programmatic tokens are minted via TMDS by default, (2) Audit records show token provenance (issuer, parent token, SSO session id, requested scopes), (3) We can rotate underlying signing keys without immediate app-level downtime, (4) A migration path exists for high-risk long-lived keys to be replaced or escrowed.
acceptance_criteria: TMDS API endpoints: /mint, /exchange, /revoke implemented and live in staging
Tokens minted include structured metadata fields: issuer, parent_key, scope_list, ttl_seconds, human_label
Audit events emitted to our ELK with JSON schema v2 and linked to SSO session id when applicable
Runtime enforces scope restrictions when presented token tries to access resources outside its scopes
Admin console can list tokens by owner, scope, label and perform bulk revocation
System supports rotation of signing key with zero-downtime introspection via key IDs and gradual rollover
decision_log: 2025-02-20: Chose JSON Web Tokens (JWS) with key id header for portable verification; reason: existing SDKs already accept JWS and we want inspectability without DB hit for read-heavy auth checks.

2025-02-24: Decided to store token metadata in a write-optimized ledger (immutable append) rather than as primary source of truth; reason: performance and audit tamper-evidence. Token validation uses header+signature + optional ledger lookup for revocation/attenuation.

2025-03-01: Opted for default TTLs by scope class (service:1h, ephemeral-cli:15m, embed-keys:30d) with ability to request custom TTLs for privileged roles; reason: balance security and usability for migration

rollout_plan: Phase 0 (staging): TMDS behind feature flag; all new engineering-created tokens minted via TMDS. Duration: 2 weeks.
Phase 1 (beta): Opt-in by teams; console shows 'migratable keys' list and one-click exchange flow for services. Duration: 4 weeks.
Phase 2 (enforced): New token creation for high-risk scopes only via TMDS; warning banners and migration guides. Duration: 6 weeks.
Phase 3 (full): Deprecate legacy root tokens; automated escrow/retirement for keys not migrated. Duration: gated on audit coverage and SSO integration.
Rollback: feature flags for minting and enforcement; emergency revoke endpoint with global fanout via pubsub
